clue.text: Almost oust one conservative where something is safely kept

indicators.note: almost means the word is cut short by its final letter here

parts.note: to oust a ruler is to depose them
the Roman numeral for one is I
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A bid to remove a Tory MP ends up near a vault where valuables are stored.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' drops the last letter of the verb for oust; 'one' and 'conservative' then supply the usual numeral and party abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A repository or storehouse is a place where goods are deposited for safe keeping.

clue.text: Challenge shows one's fed up with one's awful acne

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word fed is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: taken as written
one is I, the Roman numeral

indicators.note: awful signals that the letters of acne are spoilt and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone sick of their dreadful spots puts on a show of bravado.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns FED into DEF in this down clue; 'awful' rearranges ACNE into ANCE. The first 'one's' joins the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Defiance is open resistance, the act of challenging authority.

clue.text: Forced painter to be relevant

indicators.note: forced suggests the letters of painter are wrenched into a new order

explanation.surface: An artist made to work against their will must justify themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: To pertain is to relate or belong to the matter in hand.

clue.text: Radical haircut?

parts.note: a shock is a thick mass of hair, so a drastic way of dealing with one is a pun on the harsh medical therapy

explanation.surface: A barber offers a dramatic new style.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase names an extreme therapy, once electric shocks; read literally it is something done to a shock of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Electroconvulsive therapy is a drastic remedy, and the clue reads it as treating a shock, a thick head of hair.

clue.text: Jumbo was tried out by this person

definitions.text: Jumbo was tried out by this person

parts.words: Jumbo was tried out by this person
parts.note: Jumbo sounds like the circus elephant but here means a jumbo jet, which someone has to fly on trial before passengers board

explanation.surface: Someone once put a famous elephant through its paces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jumbo' suggests an elephant; it is a jumbo jet, a Boeing 747, and the person who flies a new aircraft first is the one wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: Aviators employed to fly new aircraft and assess them are given this job title.

clue.text: Make greatly annoyed about fellow's weapon

indicators.note: about means the first piece wraps round the second

parts.note: to rile someone is to make them very annoyed
F is the dictionary abbreviation for fellow

explanation.surface: A man's gun is a source of real irritation to his neighbours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts F inside RILE.
explanation.definitionFit: A rifle is a long-barrelled firearm.

clue.text: One bishop is a flighty type

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I
B is the chess notation for bishop

explanation.surface: A single churchman proves to be rather frivolous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flighty type' suggests a scatterbrain; it means a creature that flies.
explanation.definitionFit: The ibis is a wading bird, and birds are creatures of flight.

clue.text: Money which is awarded to runner-up?

explanation.surface: Second place in a race earns some cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Coins of the realm are often called silver, and a second-placed competitor receives the silver medal.

clue.text: Breakaway cliques suggesting US prog.

parts.note: break up the letters of a word meaning cliques and they splinter into US PROG

explanation.surface: Dissident factions hint at an American progressive rock band.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as an instruction: splinter the six-letter word for cliques and you get US PROG, the clue's own letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Factions that break away from a larger party are dissident cliques.

clue.text: In favour of attempt to exercise restraint

parts.note: to be for something is to be in favour of it
a go is an attempt or try

explanation.surface: Supporting a try at self-control.
explanation.definitionFit: To forgo something is to refrain from it, doing without by an act of self-denial.

clue.text: Pleads effectively about frequently being moderate

indicators.note: about means the anagrammed letters surround the other piece
effectively suggests the letters of pleads are made to work in a new arrangement

parts.note: oft is an old word for often, frequently

explanation.surface: Someone making a strong case often has to tone things down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'effectively' is an unusual anagram signal, making the letters work afresh; 'about' tells you the rearranged letters surround the word for frequently.
explanation.definitionFit: To soft-pedal is to play down or tone down, making something less extreme.

clue.text: Axe Liberal from sect

indicators.note: from tells us the one letter is taken away from the other word

parts.note: a cult is a religious sect

explanation.surface: A religious group expels its liberal member.
explanation.definitionFit: To axe something is to cut it, as with spending or jobs.

clue.text: A support could be taken so in surprise

definitions.text: could be taken so in surprise

parts.note: to back someone is to support them

explanation.surface: Being given help can leave one startled.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition fills a gap: someone surprised is 'taken ___'.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'taken aback' means startled or disconcerted.

clue.text: Much made of this inept duel fought

indicators.note: a fight makes a mess, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Commentators make a great deal of a clumsy swordfight.
explanation.definitionFit: Plenitude is abundance, a great amount of something.

clue.text: Cold buildings need this reduced for Switzerland

explanation.surface: Chilly Swiss chalets need their heating turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: Abbreviated, the answer is CH, which is also the international code for Switzerland.
explanation.definitionFit: A home warmed by radiators fed from one boiler has this system, abbreviated CH, the same letters as Switzerland's code.

clue.text: This can be applied until you are blue in the face

definitions.text: This can be applied until you are blue in the face

parts.words: This can be applied until you are blue in the face
parts.note: blue in the face usually means exhausted from effort; here it means literally coloured blue by make-up around the eyes

explanation.surface: Someone keeps trying something until they are exhausted.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom for futile effort is read literally: a blue cosmetic applied near the eyes.
explanation.definitionFit: Coloured cosmetic brushed onto the eyelids can literally make a face blue.

clue.text: Sewers heading south will be without point

indicators.note: heading south means moving downwards, so in this down clue the letter goes at the bottom

parts.note: a sewer here is one that sews, such as a needle

explanation.surface: Drains running downhill serve no purpose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sewers' looks like drains; it means things that sew.
explanation.definitionFit: Needless means unnecessary, serving no point or purpose.

clue.text: Perhaps net & fan for precocious brat

parts.note: the letters of these two words can be made from a French word for child when it is treated terribly

explanation.surface: An unruly child is given a fishing net and an electric fan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' warns that the answer read as wordplay, ENFANT arranged terribly, gives NET and FAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A French phrase for an outrageous young person who shocks with unconventional behaviour.

clue.text: Ron's lit up this facial feature

indicators.note: up as in stirred up signals the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the name with its S counted as a letter

explanation.surface: Ron lights a cigarette and it goes straight up his nose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' rearranges the letters of RONS and LIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Each opening of the nose is one, a feature of the face.

clue.text: Mineral making British exit unusual with gold in

indicators.note: in means the gold goes inside the other letters
unusual signals the letters of exit appear in an unusual order

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: Brexit with gold thrown in would be an odd outcome.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface evokes Brexit; 'unusual' rearranges the exit and 'in' slips gold's chemical symbol between the British abbreviation and those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Bauxite is the clay-like ore from which aluminium is extracted.

clue.text: Fellow in awfully fusty surroundings is strait-laced

indicators.note: in tells us the abbreviation for fellow goes inside the rearranged letters
awfully suggests the letters of fusty are mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: A man living in a musty old house is rather prim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awfully' rearranges FUSTY to STUFY, 'in' places F among them; 'surroundings' supports the containment.
explanation.definitionFit: Stuffy describes someone prim and conventional, narrow-minded in manner.

clue.text: Gauge light for cricket game

parts.note: to gauge is to measure or test
a match gives a light

explanation.surface: Checking the light meter before play at a cricket ground.
explanation.walkthrough: A TEST MATCH is an international cricket game lasting up to five days.
explanation.definitionFit: International five-day fixtures between national sides are given this name in cricket.

clue.text: Office worker gets nothing in time

parts.note: a temp is a temporary office worker
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A clerk achieves nothing during working hours.
explanation.definitionFit: In music tempo is the speed or time of a piece.

clue.text: About in a circle

explanation.definitionFit: Round means approximately, as in round about ten, and also circular or going in a ring.

clue.text: Ring after publicity eaus-es a fuss

indicators.note: after means the ring comes behind the publicity in the answer

parts.note: an ad is an advertisement, publicity
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A phone call following an advertisement stirs up commotion.
explanation.definitionFit: Ado is bustle or fuss, as in much ado about nothing.

clue.text: English men upset about one taken in by car maker -Henry?

indicators.note: taken in by means the inner letters sit inside the car maker's name

parts.note: Ford is the American car manufacturer

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters wrap round the numeral
upset tells us the letters of men are knocked over into a different order

parts.note: one is A, as in a single thing

explanation.surface: Englishmen upset over a single model made by Henry Ford.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is an example: Henry is a given name, so someone forenamed Henry is called that first; Henry Ford, the car maker, is the hint.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry is a first name, so one given that name before the surname is first-named as such.

clue.text: Capable of being employed as upper-class roofing material

parts.note: a tile covers roofs

explanation.surface: A posh slate can be put to good use.
explanation.definitionFit: Utile is an old word for useful, serviceable.

clue.text: Shout of Shetlander from here?

explanation.walkthrough: Yell is one of the Shetland Islands, off the north of Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: A loud cry is one sense; the other is an island in the Shetland group from which a Shetlander may come.

clue.text: Oilskins we set out in spoils

indicators.note: in means the rearranged letters go inside the word for spoils

parts.note: food that spoils sours

indicators.note: out suggests the letters of we and set are spread out in a new order

explanation.surface: Waterproofs set out by us get ruined.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges the two little words, and 'in' places them inside a verb meaning spoils, as milk does.
explanation.definitionFit: Sou'westers are waterproof oilskin hats worn by sailors and fishermen.
